result.title: VTT: Reading Vehicle Size and Powertrain Type from Motion Trajectory Across Unseen Car Models
result.summary: Vehicle size and powertrain information can enrich trajectory data for traffic analysis and simulation. We present VTT, a dataset and benchmark for identifying these attributes from motion and controller area network (CAN) signals across unseen car models. The dataset contains 9,062 drives, about 3,950 h, from 1,431 vehicles and 174 car models. It provides three footprint-based size classes, powertrain labels, and evaluation on unseen car models and unseen drivers. Using 60-s windows, we compare four sequence architectures, statistical features and physical features proposed by large language models. Training with auxiliary physical targets, data augmentation and task-specific weighting raises drive-level macro-F1 to 92.6-93.0% for battery-electric versus combustion vehicles and from 62.9% to 67.1% for size classification. On public logs from 4,061 additional drivers, the full-input model identifies powertrain correctly for 86 of 88 car models; size accuracy is 63.2%, close to the internal vehicle-level result of 63.5%. Physical-feature analysis links powertrain recognition to deceleration behaviour and size recognition to steering response. Errors near size-class boundaries and limited gains from longer observations highlight the importance of label resolution and training-fleet coverage for cross-model generalisation.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出 VTT 数据集与基准，用车辆运动轨迹与 CAN 信号在未见车型上识别车身尺寸等级与动力类型，并比较多种序列模型、统计与物理特征。
AI.relevance_reason: 属汽车轨迹属性分类任务，既不涉及视觉语言模型的内部表示与推理状态生成，也未讨论证据筛选、停止决策或 latent 内容的使用，缺乏可供核查的 LVR 联系。
